Question
========
What is part of the ISA (Instruction Set Architecture)?


Answerlist
----------
* Instructions of the CPU
* Pipeline stages
* Number of caches
* Number of registers

Solution
========
The ISA is the contract between the hardware and the software: what the programmer can name and use. Everything that is only an implementation choice of a given chip is microarchitecture, not ISA.

Answerlist
----------
* 1. The instructions and their encoding are the core of the ISA.
* 0. The pipeline depth is a microarchitectural choice, invisible in the ISA.
* 0. The cache hierarchy is a microarchitectural choice.
* 1. The architectural registers are named by the instructions, so they belong to the ISA.
